subject.title: [Feature]: Cron job output routing — hard-coded destination for job results (file, channel, session)

question: Should OpenClaw add a first-class cron output-target contract, and if so which target types, security rules, and partial-failure/status semantics should be part of the supported API?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the requested fix adds a new config/API surface plus framework-owned file, channel, and cross-session writes, so automation should not choose the permanent product and security policy.

options.title: Design One Canonical Output Contract
options.body: Define one cron output contract for file, channel, session, silent, fallback, and status behavior before implementation so related subsets do not diverge.

options.title: Split Into Narrower Trackers
options.body: Keep this as an umbrella but require separate maintainer-approved issues for file output, session output, channel fan-out, and default delivery before coding each part.

options.title: Reject Framework-Owned Output Targets
options.body: Keep current prompt/tool-driven routing and improve docs or diagnostics instead, avoiding new file/session/channel write authority in cron config.

recommendation.title: Design One Canonical Output Contract
recommendation.body: Define one cron output contract for file, channel, session, silent, fallback, and status behavior before implementation so related subsets do not diverge.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has recent history in the cron delivery dispatch boundary and prior triage context on this canonical tracker, making them the best available routing owner for the product/security choice.
